class.name: NetwChannelBook
class.brief_description: What one channel is registered as: the handler its frames are given to, and whether they wait for a route this peer does not know yet.
class.description: Both facts are one row because they are one registration. Held apart, a caller can unregister the handler and leave the deferral behind, and the frames that answer to it park against a handler that is gone. A channel is registered through one of two doors, and the door it came through is what it answers to. An entity channel carries a route and its handler takes the entity that route names; a peer-scoped channel carries no route and its handler takes only the payload and the sender. The two lanes read through different accessors, so a row registered for one lane is never handed a frame from the other, and re-registering through the other door moves the row rather than leaving two. [codeblock] book.register_channel(channel, handler, true) # entity lane book.register_protocol(channel, handler) # peer-scoped lane book.defers(channel) # a frame for an unknown route waits book.handler_of(channel) # who it is given to when the route binds [/codeblock]

method.name: defers
method.description: Whether a frame on [param channel] for an unknown route waits for it rather than being dropped. An unregistered channel defers nothing, because there would be nothing to hand the frame to when the route arrived. A peer-scoped channel defers nothing either, because it names no route to wait for.

method.name: handler_of
method.description: The entity-lane handler registered for [param channel], or an empty [Callable]. A channel registered through [method register_protocol] answers here with an empty [Callable], because its handler does not take an entity.

method.name: protocol_handler_of
method.description: The peer-scoped handler registered for [param channel], or an empty [Callable]. The mirror of [method handler_of]: a channel registered through [method register_channel] answers here with an empty [Callable].

method.name: register_channel
method.description: Registers [param handler] for [param channel] on the entity lane and answers whether it replaced an earlier registration. Re-registering replaces both facts together, so a handler and a deferral can never describe different registrations.

method.name: register_protocol
method.description: Registers [param handler] for [param channel] on the peer-scoped lane and answers whether it replaced an earlier registration. A peer-scoped row never defers, so this is the one door that takes no deferral.

method.name: settle_protocol
method.description: Answers whether every peer-scoped channel the wire declares holds a handler, and warns naming each one that does not. A session that settles with a hole here would drop that channel's frames in silence for the rest of its life, so the hole is reported once, at settle, rather than discovered as missing traffic. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when any is missing.

method.name: size
method.description: How many channels are registered, counting both lanes.

method.name: unregister_channel
method.description: Drops [param channel]'s registration from whichever lane holds it, and answers whether there was one. The deferral goes with the handler.
